thread:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] ALB eu-west-1-edge (alb-prod-xyz) marked 42 targets unhealthy in 2m and started deregistering. Pager: https://pager.company/INC-8321

sam: seeing it now, looking into target logs and node status.

maria: same, canary and prod edges impacted. any recent net changes?

sam: pulled ALB health logs, lots of connection resets rather than 5xx. example line: client_ip=3.123.45.67 target_ip=10.2.3.45 status_code=0 reason=connection_reset

jin: ran tcpdump on node ip-10-2-3-45 and see many incoming SYNs from ALB HC IPs and immediate RSTs back. looks like local stack is rejecting them.

maria: i did push a quick iptables-based rate limit to edge nodes earlier to knock down noisy scanners (hashlimit). trying to remember exact rule.

sam: can you paste the rule?

maria: the rule we pushed via cf-template: 

```
iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 8080 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -m hashlimit --hashlimit-name ALB_HC --hashlimit-above 50/min --hashlimit-mode srcip -j REJECT
```

maria: it was intended to cut repetitive connections from a single source.

lisa: ALB healthcheck IPs come in bursts and sometimes reuse source IPs/ports; hashlimit on srcip will start rejecting legitimate HC bursts. that matches the timing.

jin: confirmed counters on node: `sudo iptables -L ALLOW -v --line-numbers` shows rule hitcounts climbing (pkts: 1200) and many REJECTs with icmp-unreach. syslog contains lines: "kernel: iptables: REJECT IN=eth0 OUT= MAC=..."

sam: on one node i temporarily removed the rule and pushed a quick firewall allow for the ALB HC CIDR -> target moved to healthy within 30s. verified with `aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn ...`

maria: wow, that explains it. i scoped the rule too wide. my bad.

lisa: plan: 1) rollback the hashlimit rule across the edge ASG now, 2) add whitelist for ALB healthcheck CIDRs or use --hashlimit-htable-size/per-target finer tuning, 3) add unit tests that simulate ALB bursty HC patterns, 4) alert on iptables REJECT rate to catch regressions.

sam: i'll open a PR for the whitelist/safer hashlimit and a runbook change. also we should add a canary that runs health checks from ALB IP ranges during staging.

deploy-bot: runbook "revert-alb-hashlimit" started against asg-edge-nodes (12 instances). status: in-progress.

lisa: reverted rule on 12 nodes via SSM runbook. monitoring: ALB targets recovered across all AZs, deregistration stopped.

sam: follow-up tasks: update CF template, add ALB CIDR allowlist and lower hashlimit threshold to 200/min or switch to per-src+per-dst pair. also add a Grafana panel for iptables REJECTs/sec.

maria: i'm writing the PR now, will include test harness and changelog note. sorry for the pager noise.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-8321 marked resolved. Postmortem required?

sam: yes, short postmortem and link to PR in the doc.

-- end of thread --
